title: Arbiter402
tagline: Sub-second conditional micro-escrow & zero-hallucination adjudication for machine commerce.
description:
Arbiter402 is an autonomous, sub-second conditional micro-escrow and deterministic ground-truth adjudication protocol built for the machine economy. While demonstrated on high-stakes DeFi indexing as its reference implementation, the protocol is fundamentally modular and generalizable to any verifiable machine-to-machine compute task.

Why Human-in-the-Loop Fails for AI Agents:
Traditional escrow and human arbitration (e.g., Kleros, multi-sig signers) are completely infeasible for machine-to-machine commerce:
• Cost Inversion: AI agents execute micro-transactions ($0.05 - $1.00). Paying human jurors $10+ to review a $0.20 dispute is an immediate economic failure.
• Latency Destruction: Human dispute cycles take days or weeks. An autonomous agent making automated market actions needs settlement in seconds, not days.
• The LLM Trap: Using an LLM to judge another LLM introduces stochastic drift, hallucinations, and prompt injection. Machine commerce demands deterministic mathematical ground truth.

How Arbiter402 Solves It:
• Sub-Second Micro-Escrow: Buyer agents lock micro-escrows into ArbiterEscrow.sol on Hedera EVM (~0.84s finality, ~$0.007 gas fee) via HTTP 402 and MCP tool-calling.
• Zero-Hallucination Adjudication: When deliverables are contested, our referee queries The Graph's decentralized indexing network to evaluate mathematical invariants (e.g., Uniswap v3 VWAP over verified block ranges) directly from raw onchain swap logs.
• ERC-8004 Machine Reputation: Lost disputes trigger atomic refunds and slash rogue agents by -50 points onchain, while honest completions award +5 points.
• Immutable HCS Audit Trail: Signed ECDSA audit proofs are anchored to Hedera Consensus Service for public verifiability on HashScan.
how_its_made:
Arbiter402 brings together Hedera EVM, Hedera Consensus Service (HCS), The Graph, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) into a unified, hardened machine-commerce pipeline:

• Hedera EVM Smart Contracts: We developed and deployed ArbiterEscrow.sol (0.0.10520281) and ERC8004ReputationRegistry.sol (0.0.10520278) on Hedera Testnet (Chain ID 296), both 100% verified on Sourcify with Exact Match. Hedera's ~0.84s finality and fixed sub-cent fees enable high-frequency micro-escrow transactions that are cost-prohibitive on L1.

• Hedera Consensus Service (HCS): Every dispute adjudication generates a tamper-proof audit payload containing the job specification hash, deliverable hash, ground-truth value, error delta, and the referee's ECDSA signature, permanently anchored to HCS Topic 0.0.10520952 with nanosecond consensus timestamps and stored in the contract's auditLogUri.

• The Graph Decentralized Oracle: To eliminate subjective LLM arbitration, our referee queries The Graph’s decentralized network for raw Uniswap v3 swap events (amount0, amount1, sqrtPriceX96). It deterministically computes the true Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) across the requested block window to evaluate deviations against basis-point contract tolerances.

• Bazantic MCP Recipe & HTTP 402: Built with @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, our recipe server exposes standardized tools (adjudicate_escrow_dispute, verify_agent_reputation) allowing autonomous agents in Claude, Cursor, and LangChain to negotiate escrows and trigger dispute settlements natively over standardized HTTP 402 headers.

• Security Hardening: We engineered a cryptographic deliverable substitution defense (pre-flight checks ensure payloads match onchain keccak256 hashes), push-to-pull fallback queues (pendingWithdrawals) that immunize against denial-of-service reverts, and liveness safety valves for uncontested claims and expired deadlines.
auto_summary: A Hedera-based escrow system uses smart contracts, an MCP server, and Graph queries to automate dispute resolution for machine-to-machine tasks.
